summary: Dependency-confusion beacon on @grabcad scope posts host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package publishes under the @grabcad organization scope but ships only a beacon script and a Proxy-based no-op shim as its main export. On npm install, the postinstall hook runs `node beacon.cjs`; on require, index.js invokes `beacon.fire()`. Both paths POST a payload containing the installer's hostname, install path (__dirname), current working directory, Node.js version, and package name to the hardcoded bare-IPv4 endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The exported module is a Proxy returning no-op functions for every property access, so consumers that resolve this package in place of a private internal @grabcad package link successfully but receive no real functionality. The combination of scope-squatting an organization namespace, a non-first-party bare-IP collector, install-time and import-time execution, and a stub shim is the standard dependency-confusion reconnaissance pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
